newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday due to fresh money supply from the redemption of recently-matured state debt, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 9.5 percent from 10.00 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market jumped to 9.7 million lots from 4.1 million on Wednesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
About 30 billion yuan worth of state debt is maturing in April and their redemption has added supply on the repo market.

The repo rates opened up and stayed at high levels early in the session on Thursday due to rises on the domestic A share markets and two new A share issues on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, traders said.
But significant money supply increases on the repo market quickly depressed the rates and made them close down.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to consolidate down on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Thursday on a technical correction after sharp gains in the past two days, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 117.60 yuan from 117.85 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.6 million lots from 2.5 million lots.
Despite Thursday's fall, traders said sentiment was good due to high yields for the existing contracts and liquidity from matured state debt redemption flowing into the spot market.
The contracts have annual yields of around 10 percent on average, against 7.47 percent for one-year bank deposits.
"The technical correction will continue tomorrow but prices are likely to recover early next week," one trader said.
